A_target.statement:
Let $X$ be a non-negative integer-valued [[Definition:Random Variable|random variable]] with $\expect X > 0$.
Then:
:$\map \Pr {X = 0} \le \dfrac {\var X} {\expect X^2}$

B_source.statement:
Let $X$ be a [[Definition:Random Variable|random variable]] with finite variance and $a > 0$.
Then:
:$\map \Pr {\size {X - \expect X} \ge a} \le \dfrac {\var X} {a^2}$

validity_conditions: X >= 0, so the event {X = 0} implies |X - E[X]| = E[X] >= E[X], placing {X=0} inside the Chebyshev event with a = E[X].
E[X] > 0 so the bound Var(X)/E[X]^2 is well-defined.
Monotonicity of probability then gives P(X=0) <= P(|X-E[X]| >= E[X]).
proof_plan:
By [[Chebyshev's Inequality]] with $a = \expect X$:
:$\map \Pr {\size {X - \expect X} \ge \expect X} \le \dfrac {\var X} {\expect X^2}$

If $X = 0$ then $\size {X - \expect X} = \expect X$.
Hence:
:$\set {X = 0} \subseteq \set {\size {X - \expect X} \ge \expect X}$

By [[Probability Measure is Monotone|monotonicity]]:
:$\map \Pr {X = 0} \le \map \Pr {\size {X - \expect X} \ge \expect X}$

Chaining:
:$\map \Pr {X = 0} \le \dfrac {\var X} {\expect X^2}$
which is the [[Definition:Second Moment Method|second moment method]].
{{qed}}
